decision.question: Does comparison of the source and edited images establish that the source mug has been relocated to the right of the headphones?
decision.criteria: Pass when the combined visual evidence sufficiently supports correspondence between the source mug and an edited mug positioned to the right of the edited headphones. Compare both edited candidates explicitly: the source mug has a broad light-blue body, blue interior with a dark lower region, and a left-facing handle; the right candidate has a dark interior, smaller and more tapered body, and right-facing handle; the left candidate has a light interior and different appearance. Weigh interior appearance as a meaningful comparative cue together with body proportions, rim, handle geometry, surface appearance and relative scale. Account for the substantially changed framing, lighting and possible rotation; differences in color, scale or handle orientation are not automatic disproof or independent failures. Neither dark interior alone nor right-side placement alone establishes identity. Explain why the full cue combination supports one candidate over the other, or why it remains inconclusive. Inspect the former mug location for recognizable residual structure, but do not infer retention or successful removal from the far-left blue blur alone. Fail only when the evidence establishes that the source mug remains left of the headphones or otherwise has not reached the requested right-side position. Return unknown when correspondence or resulting placement cannot be established; absence of proof of completion is not proof of failure. Calibrate confidence to the strength and conflict of the visual evidence rather than reporting strong confidence in an unresolved identity judgment.
decision.binding: Target: the light-blue mug with a left-facing handle in the source image. Reference: the headphones in each image. Compare the source mug with both edited candidates: the pale mug left of the headphones and the dark-interior mug right of the headphones. Inspect the far-left blue blurred patch only as ambiguous possible residual evidence, not as an identified mug. Assess which candidate, if either, corresponds to the relocated source mug using the combined visual cues. Compare object-relative placement with the edited headphones, allowing for changed framing, scale and headphone arrangement rather than relying on raw pixel coordinates.
